name: Eastern Woodlands (1750s)
tooltip: Clothing of the Native nations of the Northeast, such as the Haudenosaunee, Lenape, Shawnee and Wabanaki, in the mid-1700s: wool and linen trade cloth, quillwork and silverwork.
review: This set shows the dress of living nations. It follows the costume bible (sections 3.1-3.8) and has not been reviewed by the nations concerned; paid review of meshes, names and lore by their cultural or historic-preservation offices is needed before public release, and consultants should be credited.
note: Written by tools/character/garments/woodlands/_set_catalog.py from the catalog fragments (ew_*.json, written by the generators); the merged assets/character/catalog.json is the runtime source for items. Presets change the outfit only (never body, skin, face, eyes or hair); colour keys are zone names.

ew_armbands.description: A pair of broad silver bands worn on the upper arms above the elbows, over the shirt sleeves or on the bare arm.
ew_armbands.history: Silver arm bands above and below the elbow were widely worn (Smith [P1], Heckewelder [P2], Jones [R2]; Six Nations silverwork [M11]).

ew_matchcoat.name: Wool blanket (matchcoat)
ew_matchcoat.description: A stroud or duffel blanket worn as a matchcoat: wrapped round the hips and belted, the upper part brought across the body and over the left shoulder, leaving the right arm free.
ew_matchcoat.history: A rectangle of stroud about 60 x 65 inches, blue most common, or a white duffel blanket with coloured end stripes, wrapped or belted round the body [R3][R17]; dress versions were edged with ribbon and set with brooches [P2].
